question:
A user is a member of two groups: Group A applies a Microsoft 365 E3 license with the Exchange Online service plan enabled, and Group B applies a Microsoft 365 E3 license with the Exchange Online service plan explicitly disabled. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, the user's license status shows a "Problem" indicator for a service plan.

What is the most accurate description of the resulting state, and how should an administrator resolve it?

options.text: Group-based licensing resolves plan-level conflicts by disabling the conflicting service plan for that user, and admins can inspect the conflict on the user's "Licenses" blade to decide whether to adjust the group assignments
The two group license assignments cancel each other out entirely, and the user receives no Microsoft 365 E3 license at all until the conflict is fixed
Group-based licensing does not support any per-service-plan customization, so both groups must assign the exact same set of enabled service plans
The conflict can only be resolved by removing group-based licensing entirely and assigning the license directly to the user

explanation:
When multiple group license assignments provide the same product but disagree on whether a specific service plan is enabled or disabled, Microsoft Entra ID's group-based licensing engine resolves it automatically — the disabled setting effectively takes precedence for that plan — and surfaces a "Problem licenses" indicator so an administrator can review exactly which service plan is in conflict and adjust one of the group assignments if the resulting state isn't what was intended.

**Why not the other options:**
- **"No license at all"** — the user still receives the underlying product license (Microsoft 365 E3); the conflict is scoped to the specific service plan setting, not the whole product.
- **"No per-service-plan customization at all"** — group-based licensing explicitly supports enabling/disabling individual service plans within a license assigned to a group; the scenario's conflict only arises because that customization exists and differs between the two groups.
- **"Must remove group-based licensing entirely"** — an admin can resolve the conflict by adjusting the conflicting group's service-plan configuration or group membership; removing group-based licensing altogether is a far more drastic step than required.
